text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav state and economic delegation headed by foreign trade minister Borislav Vukovic arrives in Bonn on a German tour to present Yugoslavia's economy.
- Yugoslavia plans to go ahead with trade liberalisation from January 1998, says Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Borislav Vukovic.
NASA BORBA
- Cooperation with the international war crimes tribunal dominated talks between U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in Belgrade.
- Doctors will continue their strike this week because the Serbian government has not lived up to an agreement reached with medical workers trade union to pay outstanding wages by the end of May.
- Yugoslav delegation left for Brussels to attend new round of succession talks on the ex-Yugoslav federation.
- Serbia consumes 95,000 tonnes of wheat per month and its reserves will be exhausted within 2-1/2 months, independent analysts said.
- Yugoslav agriculture ministry and farmers to reach an agreement on Monday on guaranteed wheat price which expected to remain unchanged at 0.9 dinars per kilo.
- Hungarian firm Fiorentini Hungary Kft expected to be chosen at an international tender for financing construction of a $2 million worth stretch of a gas pipeline in Sremska Mitrovica.
- Serbian inspectors confiscate large quantity of goods at Belgrade flea market over the weekend. The flea market will remain closed until status of salesmen is resolved.
BORBA
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic said deflation of prices expected in May. Price and currency stability remain basic goals of the government's economic policy.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Textile, meat, fruit, vegetables and steel goods producers will benefit most from EU trade preferentials, Serbian Chamber of Commerce official Gradimir Cvetkovic said.
- Trial of a 15-member Kosovo Albanian terrorist group opens in Pristina court on Tuesday on charges of having killed three Serbian policemen and one civilian between 1992 and 1996.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- New Democracy (ND) will participate in forthcoming elections in coalition with the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) and the Yugoslav Left (JUL) like at the previous elections.
GRADJANIN

- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic expected to leave office in early September while the new minister for private enteprise Milan Beko and vice-president of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) Dusan Matkovic are listed as possible successors.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- The Montenegrin president has no legal and constitutional authority to influence the legal and constitutional competences of the government, said Justice Minister Dusko Lalicevic.
- Slovenian company Andino and German company Noel, refusing to accept only guarantees of Yugoslav banks, broke off a $5 million contract on reconstruction of hydro-electric power plant Perucica.

- Private tour-operator Mercur from Budva bought a 51 percent stake of the construction material producer Racica from Tivat. Racica workers own 32 percent and three state funds 17 percent of the company's stake. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
